messages.author: 7c31dd3eaed5edbe
messages.subject: Load PDF into R
parts:
Quick question Rists: Has anyone loaded an indexed (word searchable)
PDF file into R? If not directly into R, by way of another program,
possibly a text editor or spreadsheet software? I'd like to produce
concordances and frequency lists from texts stored in PDF format. I
tried to simply load a PDF file into R with scan(), but got a bunch of
code stuff (maybe hex code?) like this:

\x9e\xc9\xea\031:\xec\x8db\001\xf1\xc7F\xa5\xa9

Maybe I can convert this "junk" to the words that they produce in a
PDF file? Any ideas? Thanks. Earl Brown

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Load PDF into R
parts:
On Linux, no problem. Within R, just do this:

system("pdftotext '/home/stgries/Desktop/2005_Dąbrowska_Lieven.pdf' xyz.txt")

Now, xyz.txt can be loaded with scan as usual ... Done. Other OSs? Who
knows ... ;-)

HTH,
STG

messages.author: dc7de9381942e07b
messages.subject: Re: Load PDF into R
parts:
Hi Earl,I had a similar problem working with a corpus of 180 theses
and dissertations all in .pdf format. Using a pdf to text converter, I
ended up converting each of the files one bye one. This solution is
probably very elementary, though, and it'd be great to learn how to do
it in an automatic fashion.

An issue Stefan has brought to my attention was the fact that when I
converted the files to txt, the footnotes got in the middle of the
main text, which means I lose a lot of data when looking for
concordances and contexts.

I still don't know how to solve this problem, so for now I'm using the
corpus despite of the "footnote interruptions"...

parts:
At the very least you could merge all pdfs using Combine PDFs (Mac)
or Adobe (Windows) or some other tool, and then do a single
conversion from that huge pdf to a huge text file. In Combine PDFs,
the merging feature is simply a matter of drag and drop into the
window then hitting merge, so merging 180 shouldn't take any longer
than merging 2, except computationally ;)
Alex

messages.author: 7c31dd3eaed5edbe
messages.subject: Re: Load PDF into R
parts:
Success! It worked! I downloaded and installed the pdftotext function
that JeridF suggested and have successfully converted several PDF
files to text files and then loaded them into R. I'm not sure if it's
this pdftotext function I just downloaded or the XPDF I previously
downloaded, as the pdftotext function is also in XPDF. In any case, I
can now convert PDF to text. Here's the R code I used, looking at
Stefan's, if you're interested (possibly Fernanda and others):

system("/usr/local/bin/pdftotext '/Users/brow2662/Documents/
Bybee_Eddington_2006.pdf' /Users/brow2662/Documents/ByEd06.txt")

by.ed<-scan(file="/Users/brow2662/Documents/ByEd06.txt", what="char",
sep="\n")

Thank you all. Earl Brown

On Nov 8, 5:21 am, Earl Brown <earlkris...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Fernanda, your question made me think about how I might go about
> trying to preserve the file names on concordance results after
> converting files from PDF to text. Here's what I wrote in answer to
> that question. (Excuse the overload on detail, but that's how I write
> my scripts.) Best of luck. Earl Brown
>
> ############################
> # this section converts PDF to text and then loads each text file into
> R and search them
>
> rm(list=ls(all=T))
>
> # loads the function exact matches
> source(file="/Users/brow2662/Documents/_qclwr/fn_em2.r")
>
> # gets the file names with a .pdf extension
> file.names<-dir("/Users/brow2662/Documents/test_pdf_conversion",
> pattern=".pdf$", full.names=T)
>
> # creates a collector for all results
> all.results<-character()
>
> # defines search.term
> search.term<-"\bfrequency\b"
>
> # loop to convert PDF to text and then search for search.term
> for (i in file.names) {
>
>         # progress report
>         cat("Working on ", basename(i), " ", sep="")
>
>         # gets current file name
>         current.file.name<-basename(i)
>         current.file.name<-sub("\.pdf", "", current.file.name,
> ignore.case=T, perl=T)
>
>         # sets the three arguments for the call to system()
>         function.location<-"/usr/local/bin/pdftotext"
>         input.file<-paste("'", i, "'", sep="")
>         output.file<-paste("/Users/brow2662/Documents/test_pdf_conversion/",
> current.file.name, ".txt", sep="")
>
>         # converts current PDF to text
>         system(paste(function.location, input.file, output.file, sep=" "))
>
>         # creates the pathway to the newly created text file
>         current.file.text.name<-sub(".pdf$", ".txt", i, ignore.case=T,
> perl=T)
>
>         # loads the newly created text file into R and converts it to unicode
>         current.file<-scan(file=current.file.text.name, what="char",
> sep=" ", quote="", comment.char="", quiet=T)
>         current.file<-iconv(current.file, "LATIN1", "UTF-8")
>
>         # searches the current text for search.term and gets the context
> delimited matches
>         current.results<-exact.matches(search.term, current.file, pcre=T,
> case.sens=F, characters.around=50)[[4]]
>
>         # if no hits in current file, goes to next file
>         if (length(current.results)==0) {
>                 next
>         }
>
>         # adds the current file name before the results
>         current.results<-paste(current.file.name, current.results, sep=" ")
>
>         # adds current results to all results
>         all.results<-append(all.results, current.results)
>
> } # next file
>
> # saves all results to hard drive
> cat("FILE PRE HIT FOL", all.results, file="/Users/brow2662/
> Documents/test_pdf_conversion/results_search.txt", sep=" ")
>
> # announces finish
> cat("\aAll done! ")
>
> ############################
